title: ADDENDA: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY
text:
ADDENDA: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY        23

WELCOME HOME
(1939 Reunion)

Welcome back to the old home town,
    Though changed in many ways,
Yet there are still reminders of
    Your young and happy days.
The old school house has long been gone,
    Consumed by roaring flames;
A dwelling on the campus stands
    Where once you played your games.
A more commodious structure built
    Of brick and mortar stands
Within the western boundaries
    Upon much higher lands.
It is there that you are welcome
    To meet your friends so dear,
To walk again down memory's lane
    With pals of yesteryear.
To live again those days of yore,
    When teachers sternly said,
"Those lessons must be well prepared
    Before you go to bed."

—Martha Buford May.
notes: Page 23 of appendix. Poem 'Welcome Home' written for the 1939 Reunion by Martha Buford May.
